root_cause: The datepicker updates the input value to the locale-specific format during initialization when the input gains focus, even if no date is selected. This causes the form submission to use the locale format (e.g., '10/22/2026') instead of the expected ISO format (e.g., '2026-10-22').
repair_strategy: Modify the datepicker's _initCalendar method to initialize the calendar's state from the input value without updating the input's display value. Instead, only update any bound input or display element during initialization. The main input value remains unchanged until a date is explicitly selected, preserving the ISO format for form submission unless a new date is chosen.
expected_accessibility_effect: The datepicker will no longer inadvertently change the input value when opened and closed without selecting a date, preserving the announced value and reducing unnecessary input changes that could confuse assistive technologies.
functional_risks: If the datepicker relies on the input value being updated during initialization for correct display in certain configurations (e.g., when a boundInput or displayElement is present), those elements may not update correctly.
In inline datepicker mode, the input value may not reflect programmatic changes to selectedDates until user interaction occurs.
The visual representation of the date in the input field will remain in ISO format (e.g., '2026-10-22') instead of the locale-specific format, which may be less user-friendly for sighted users.
verification_requirements: Verify that focusing the departure date input and pressing Escape does not change the input value.
Verify that submitting the form after focusing and escaping the date input yields the departure date in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).
Verify that selecting a date in the datepicker updates the input value to the selected date in ISO format.
Verify that the datepicker still functions correctly when boundInput or displayElement properties are configured.
